claims.text: Higher Ta concentrations in TiZrHfTaₓ favor a predominantly BCC structure.
Reducing Ta to 5–15 at.% destabilizes the BCC phase and causes hcp phase formation in TiZrHfTaₓ.
Rapid cooling immediately after casting suppresses equilibrium phase formation in this alloy.
Controlled annealing after rapid cooling promotes hcp precipitation within a BCC matrix.
The proposed treatment produces finely dispersed hcp precipitates embedded in a BCC matrix.
The BCC matrix becomes softer and more deformable as Ta concentration decreases.
The hcp regions are elastically stiffer than the BCC matrix.
The hcp precipitates have enhanced resistance to shear.
The hcp precipitates strengthen the alloy by acting as barriers to dislocation motion.
The BCC matrix retains ductility through transformation-induced plasticity.
A BCC/hcp dual-phase TiZrHfTaₓ alloy can provide a better strength–ductility combination than single-phase HEAs.
The proposed dual-phase alloy will improve yield strength by at least approximately 15% relative to a single-phase BCC TiZrHfTaₓ baseline.
The proposed dual-phase alloy will maintain or improve ductility relative to the single-phase baseline.
The dual-phase microstructure will produce a modest increase in Young’s modulus.
BCC/hcp interfaces will improve fracture resistance through stress redistribution and crack blunting.
The beneficial response requires an optimal Ta concentration window of 5–15 at.%.
The beneficial response requires tightly controlled cooling rate, annealing temperature, and annealing time.
Processing outside the proposed composition or heat-treatment window may create undesirable phase fractions or brittle secondary phases.
In situ thermal or diffraction monitoring will improve the reproducibility of phase development.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says ductility will be increased, whereas the predicted outcome allows ductility merely to be maintained.

The predicted outcome allows maintained ductility, but the falsification rule can be read as requiring an improvement in ductility; thus unchanged ductility is both an allowed success and a possible falsifying result.
